items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: I’ve thought a lot about Brookmeyer and Bill Holman says this too sometimes in that

ctx.x: Have you ever written a chart that did not have any improvised solos in it?

I haven’t, and I’ve thought a lot about Brookmeyer and Bill Holman says this too sometimes in that — I can’t remember which one of them it was who was saying this but hey this is my music, I want control over it, I don’t think there is the need constantly to always have improvised solos. But you know I’m generally writing for bands where it’s expected to have improvised solos and there’s great soloists, or I’m writing secondary school music and you want the students improvising. It’s critical, you know, part of…

It’s tricky because I’ve tried it one or two times and what you find is you’re writing and writing and writing and then you come up — so far I’ve got 90 seconds of music. You know we rely on improvised solos to at least give some length to the piece.
